sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with G.R. Case No.548 of 2023 pending on the file of learned J.M.F.C., Nimapara, arising out of Nimapara P.S. Case No.187 of 2023 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 342/363/365/376/506 of IPC.

3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Nimapara by order dated 09.10.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 06.08.2023 and as charge sheet has already been filed on 23.09.2023, further continuance of the Petitioner in custody is not warranted.
5.
Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
6. Perused the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim and the medical examination report.

7. Considering the tenor thereof and taking into account the filing of charge sheet and period of custody, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the Gopal Behera vs State Of Odisha ....

8. Additionally, it is directed that Petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station once every month on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.
Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the Court in seisin.
9. Further, it is directed that the Petitioner shall not in any way try to intimidate the informant and/or her family members.

10. It shall be open to the informant and/or her family members to seek variance of this order, in the event there is any threat perception.
11.
Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
